title: The Yushi Rover drives 1.6x faster, and its first run out opens an arrival card with the model turning
context: The owner, 2026-11-13: "yushi rover should move faster. And we should announced its arrival with a card showing the 3d model rotating and a brief explanation of what it does."
outcome: ROVER.speed 16 -> 26 m/s and ROVER.turn 0.8 -> 1.3 rad/s (src/content/rover.js, the owner's quote beside them). The wheels, the suspension and the belt follow the distance the drawn rover actually rolls (src/fx/rover.js ctl.update distance), and the drawn rover chases the run at 1.3x the run's speed, so the animation speeds up with no other change. THE ARRIVAL CARD: src/fx/rover-card.js (the card, its own small WebGL renderer on the card's canvas, the rover's LOD1 cloned with cloned geometry in the bestiary's tinted wireframe, turning ROVER_CARD.spin rad/s, rAF only while open and the page visible, renderer/geometry/materials disposed on close), src/domain/rover-card.js (cardWanted: a story page from its start; acceptance and ?skip= pages pass it by unless ?rovercard=1; cardDue: the rover's first run out, once, held over a live wave by the close-up gate's fight rule), the words ROVER_CARD in src/content/rover.js. It pauses the game like THE FIRST ORDERS and closes on any key, click or tap. Wired by one hook in src/fx/rover-glue.js tick (h.arrival.tick(mode !== 'idle')) and one argument in td-tab's createRoverGlue call (+1 line). On the dog's opening the first run out is the first harvest's flare, after the wave's clear, so the card opens before the watched run.
alternatives: Reuse the build board's sprite rig (one frame to an ): rejected, the owner asked for the model rotating; a still would need re-shooting every frame.
Reuse the terminal's stage: it takes the game's renderer over the paused game; a card-sized renderer of its own is less coupling and is freed whole on close.

Hold the card for the close-up gate's 'shot' and 'seat' too: rejected, the first harvest's flare starts the watched-run shot in the same frame, so the card would never open there; only a live wave holds it.
evidence: --rover (this branch, ?rovercard=1): the arrival card opened at the rover's first run out (left home 223 ms wall after F): YUSHI ROVER, 3 lines, 9,908 / 57,600 lit pixels read back off the card's canvas, 9 frames, 61 draw calls; closed: {open false, frames 24, disposed true, error null}, #rover-card gone. Screenshot .superpowers/scratch/rover-card.png.
